full_judgment:
3. It has been stated in the application praying for vacating the order arrest that this court by an order dated 10.11.2015, was pleased to admit the suit and also passed an order for arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897. But the actual facts remains that the owner of the vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOH SDN BHD handed over the defendant No.1 vessel to the defendant No.3 SOLARIS CLASSIC SDN BHD on charter party agreement dated 02.4.2014 and the said charterer subsequently entered into a ship management agreement with the plaintiff on 06.5.2014, under which the plaintiff as the ship manager, took over the charge of the defendant No.1, vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897 and employed its own crews for the vessel. The defendant vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897, arrived at Chittagong Port with RBD on 23.6.2014 but the cargo allegedly solidified due to non-maintenance of required temperature at the hold for which the consignee Bay Fishing Corporation Limited and Sabnam Vegetable Oil Industries Ltd. instituted Admiralty Suit No.26 of 2014 and Admiralty Suit No.27 of 2014, respectively in this court, claiming US$ 2,42,505.00 each as compensation and obtained order of arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897 on 22.7.2014 in those two suits. But the plaintiff although has been added as defendant No.3 in the said Admiralty Suit No.26 of 2014 and Admiralty Suit No.27 of 2014 as ship manager, faied to take any step to release the vessel. Therefore, the P&1 Club of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897, at the instance of the owner of the vessel, came to a settlement with the consignee of the cargo, who withdrew the said suit on 07.01.2015 after receiving the settled amount of US$ 71,000.00 and the order of arrest vacated. The plaintiff being the ship manager has been acting negligently by not arranged and directing the vessel to sail away from Chittagong Port, rather left the defendant No.1 vessel unattended for about two and half months. On 19.3.2015, M/S Southern Marin Services again obtained an order of arrest of the defendant vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897, by filing Admiralty Suit No. 18 of 2015 in this court for its alleged claim of US$ 22,911.248 for so-called supply of necessaries. Again the plaintiff had failed and did not take any step to prevent the vessel from being arrested or to be released from the order of arrest. On 14.9.2015, the defendant No. 4(a) applicant paid US$ 21,000.00 as full and final settlement of the claim of Southern Marine Services and got release of the vessel from the order of arrest. The plaintiff instead of taking step to arrange for said out of the vessel, thereafter, instituted the instant suit claiming it's so called management fees and obtained the order of arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel, from this court. 

 4. It has been further asserted in the application that the plaintiff did not properly manage the vessel as per the terms and condition of the Standard Shipman 98 agreement and therefore the plaintiff is not entitled to any management fee and is not entitled to any order of arrest of the defendant vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, IMO No.9528897. The plaintiff, as a ship manager, did not watch over the interest of the vessel or the ship-owner and is dishonest in that it was required to fix the vessel at the most favourable terms and to collect the freight and account for them, but the plaintiff failed to do so rather due to its negligence, the vessel has been arrested by the consignees and supplier and the plaintiff refrained from releasing the vessel and even after release of the vessel the plaintiff refrained from taking the vessel out of Bangladesh. The defendant No.1 vessel having been arrested on an from 22.06.2014 has become inoperative and as such it will need US$ 1.5 Million for repair, the plaintiff has removed some valuable equipment’s from the vessel and the defendant No. 4(a)- applicant being the vessel owner has suffered and incurred huge losses due to the negligence on the part of the plaintiff to sail away from the Chittagong Port after the first arrest. 

 5. It has been further asserted in the application that the plaintiff having failed to discharge his obligation as a ship manager under the Shipman 98 Agreement is not entitled to any decree, rather it is to pay damages to this defendant No.4(a) the owner of the vessel for every day lost freight, repairing cost of the vessel, cost of missing equipment’s crew salary, bunker, fresh water, insurance, provisions, local agents fee and watchman's fee and as such the instant Admiralty Suit is not maintainable, which has been filed with a malafide intention and ill motive just to realize an illegal gains from the vessel. Therefore, the order of arrest, dated 15.11.2015 passed by this court, is liable to be re-called and the vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR is required to be released from the order of arrest. 

 8. The learned Advocate Mr. Mohammod Hossain, appearing on behalf of the defendant No.4(a)-applicant while taken this court through the Standard Ship Management Agreement, executed on the standard form of Baltic and International Maritime Council (BIMCO) being Standard Ship Management Agreement Code Name: "Shipman 98", drew the attention of this court to different management services to be rendered by the plaintiff to the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR and strenuously argued that admittedly the plaintiff is the ship manager of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR and as a ship manager the plaintiff having the possession of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, under the Shipman 98 Agreement, is not entitled to obtain an order of arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel from this court on its instance on the ground of its so called unpaid management fees. 

 9. The learned Advocate Mr. Mohammod Hossain further drew the attention of this court to the provision of Part-2 of the Shipman 98 Agreement and strenuously argued that the definition of management services liable the ship manager to render service as to crew management, technical management, commercial management, insurance management., accounting service, sale or purchase of the vessel, bunkering and this obligation of the managers are mandatorily exercisable by the ship manager, especially Clause-4 in Part-2 of Shipman 98 format categorically defined the managers obligation which the plaintiff failed to render to the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR. 

 10. The learned Advocate Mr. Mohammod Hossain vigorously argued that the provision of payment of management fees has been stipulated in Article-8 of Part-2 of the Shipman 98 Agreement, whereupon the ship owner is liable to pay the management fees if the ship manager renders services properly under the Shipman 98 Agreement. But in the instant case the ship manager totally failed to render services in accordance with the terms and condition of the Shipman 98 Agreement and although the plaintiff, as ship manager, is liable to comply the provision of Article-7 of Part-2 of the Shipman 98 Agreement, in respect of payment of collected income to the owners of the vessel, has miserably failed to comply the same and as such since the plaintiff did not account for the income it has made all through the period of agreement, no question of any due of unpaid management fees arises at all. Therefore, the arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR at the instance of the plaintiff is a wrongful arrest which under the facts and circumstances of the case cannot be sustained and liable to be recalled by this court with an order of cost against the plaintiff. 

 13. The learned Advocate Mr. Md. Bodiuzzaman, next argued that under the admitted ship management agreement the span of service to be rendered by the plaintiff as ship manager, has been defined categorically in the Shipman 98 Agreement, which does not go beyond the management service in respect of crew management, technical management, commercial management, insurance management, accounting services, sale or purchase of the vessel, upon which the plaintiff has rendered proper services as per prevailing practice in the maritime arena and at no point of time the defendant No.4(a) has raised any allegation or complaint against the plaintiff. But now the defendant No. 4(a) with a malafide intention raised the false claim that the plaintiff is a dishonest entity or that the plaintiff has not discharged its responsibility under the Shipman 98 Agreement only to avoid the payment of unpaid ship management fees. 

 16. It appears that the plaintiff has instituted the instant suit for non-payment of different claim for an amount of BD. Tk.28,038,052.70 equivalent to US$ 350,475.65, conversion rate being BD. Tk.80 per dollar. From a plain reading of the plaint along with the application for arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR and the application filed by the defendant No.4(a) praying for vacating the order of arrest, it reveals that admittedly the plaintiff was appointed as a ship manager of the defendant NO.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR under the Standard Ship Management Agreement, being the Baltic and International Maritime Council (BIMCO) Standard Ship Management Agreement, Code Name: "Shipman 98", to act as such, on an from 21.7.2014 to 21.6.2015 and accordingly it has been claimed by the plaintiff that upon such discharge of duty as ship manager the plaintiff incurred total expenditure of US$ 2,91,716.66 equivalent to BD. Tk.23,337,332.80 in respect of supplying . Lump sum crew, Victualing cost, Stores, Spares, Repair and Maintenance, Lube Oil, for supplying the necessaries and management services to the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR. 

 17. This state of affairs has prompted this court to examine the documents Shipman 98 Agreement, a copy of which has been submitted by the plaintiff in his list of documents, wherefrom it appears that the plaintiff Neptune Ship Management (Pte.) Limited was appointed by the defendant No.3 SOLARIS CLASSIC SDN BHD under the said agreement to act as ship manager to the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR. The responsibility of the ship manager has been categorically stated the Part-1 of the Shipman 98 Agreement in Clause No.5 for crew management, Clause No.6 technical management, Clause No.9 accounting services, Clause No,10 sale or purchase of the vessel, Clause No.11 provisions, Clause No.15 annual management fee and Clause No.16 for severance cost for the crew members. These responsibilities of the ship manager have been clarified in Part-2 of the Shipman 98 Agreement. Therefore, it appears that the plaintiff is entitled under the said Shipman 98 Agreement to claim any expenses if it incurred under the said agreement against the employer, by whom the plaintiff was engaged as ship manager. Therefore, it appears that the defendant No.3 SOLARIS CLASSIC SDN BHD is responsible to reimburse the plaintiff in respect of its expenditure it incurred in managing the defendant No.1 vessel IVI.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, if the plaintiff could prove successfully that it discharged its liability under the Shipman 98 Agreement at the peremptory hearing of the suit. 

 (i) that the plaintiff being an admitted ship manager of the defendant No,1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR failed to manage the ship in proper manner, as was liable under the Shipman 98 Agreement, 

 (iii) that the plaintiff being the ship manager is not entitled to arrest the vessel which was under its possession under the Shipman 98 Agreement, on the plea that the ship managers fee was not paid and different expenditure allegedly incurred by the plaintiff was not paid. 

 Out of the aforesaid three grounds this court, at this stage of the suit, is only entitled to consider the legal question as to the status of a ship manager to obtain an order of arrest of the vessel, which was put to his possession under the Shipman 98 Agreement, leaving aside the other two grounds which practically involve the factual aspect, which have to be proved before this court by cogent evidence in the dock at the time of peremptory hearing of the suit. 

 21. It appears that the defendant No.3 has appointed the plaintiff as ship manager although an attempt has been made by the learned Advocate Mr. Md. Bodiuzzaman to prove the fact that the defendant No.3 is nothing but a sham organization under the vessel owner, the defendant No. 4(a). But at this stage of the proceeding the said argument cannot be taken into consideration for the reason that the same being the factual aspects requires evidence to be adduced before this court. But a ship manager appointed by a party is always entitled to realize its management fee or any other expenditure incurred under the said management agreement from the employer who has appointed the ship manager. Therefore, it appears that the instant proceeding is practically a proceeding in personem against the defendant No.3 who has appointed the plaintiff under the Shipman 98 Agreement. The provision of Section 4 of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 provides that subject to the provision of Section 5, the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court Division may all cases be exercised in personem. But in order to obtain an order of arrest if the plaintiff succeeds that even in action in personem the claim it has raised is a maritime lien then the plaintiff will be entitled to obtain an order of arrest against the race for which the plaintiff was employed by one of the defendant as ship manager of the vessel. But although the claim which has been raised by the plaintiff is a maritime claim, as defined under the provision of Section 3(2)(V) of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000, but in no circumstances the claim, as has been raised by the plaintiff, is a maritime lien. Therefore, in a proceeding in personem and in the absence of a claim which is a maritime lien the plaintiff is not entitled to obtain an order of arrest of the defendant No.1 vessel M.T. GAGASAN JOHOR, the race for which the plaintiff was appointed as a ship manager.
